analysis:
Examined the Autopilot changes. I found no concrete regression in the supplied text.

Busy gating: the new `autopilotBusyReasons()` in ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift covers every condition in the old inline `busy` expression. Those are model switch, advertisement in flight, shutdown, drain, reconnect, inflight work, load gate, reslice, loading/unloading/retiring, startup preload, preloads, pending advertise, MTP staging/upgrade, engine recovery, revision activation/update and native MiMo retention. The all-idle admission check is therefore not weakened. `ModelAutopilotPolicy.rejection` still receives `busy`, and `provider_busy` now carries the first reason as `detail`.

Placement adoption and holds (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift): adoption and holds are in-memory only. The basis check (lines 18-27) requires saved consent, `autopilotSettings.allows(id)` (operator selection), a resident slot, not retiring, no failed self-test and, for holds, still advertised. `withdrawInactiveAutopilotModels` (Inventory.swift:15) now spares only models that pass `autopilotAdoptionIsValid`, which also requires a non-empty weightHash and non-ordinary inventory. Serving widening is limited to resident, operator-selected, consented models. Consent revocation, selection change, unload and shutdown are reconciled before each snapshot publish (Autopilot.swift:21).

Consent privacy: the new snapshot fields (capabilities, adopted/held, busy reasons, transition stalls) are attached only with `autopilotConsented` (Autopilot.swift:57). Status `detail` is gated on consent (line 272). The busy clock is reset without consent.

Unverified:
(1) `command.holdSeconds` and `leaseSeconds` bounds are not visible. `Int64(seconds) * 1_000` and `.now.advanced(by:.seconds(seconds))` (Placement.swift:63-64) could trap on a huge coordinator-supplied value, or pin memory for a long time through `autopilotHeldWeightBytes`. The coordinator is trusted, but confirm that decoding or `ModelAutopilotPolicy` caps these values.
(2) Callers of `autopilotServesModel` and the eviction and idle-unload hold integration are not in this batch. Verify that adoption does not enable prefetch or publication.
(3) ProviderLoop+TransitionWatchdog.swift was supplied as metadata plus a truncated patch excerpt only. Its cancellation behaviour (cancelling the autopilot task on stall, `autopilotStalledCommandId`) and its interaction with partial multi-victim unloads need review.
Memory-hold effects on T-029 and T-041 are unchanged in kind.
